subject: #290 flip BLOCKER (RE-DIAGNOSED s382h): a sub DEFINED INSIDE a string eval loses the eval's captured lexicals — its own eval reads the package global
description:
RULED + FIXED s383 (Fable, commit 8a273fe on main). Ruling: NO third capture route — the proposed definition-time dynamic rebind cannot work (p-eval binds the alist by REPLACEMENT, so the first inner eval site clobbers it) and is the same scope-leak family as the reverted s382h fix. Instead the pad chain is LEXICALIZED through route 1: the compiled eval body binds %p-eval-env% once at body entry to the entry value of *p-eval-lex-alist*; every eval site emitted in eval mode appends it after its own let-bound pairs (_eval_lexical_alist, the ONE shared builder); named subs close over it; nesting threads for free. Runtime untouched; file-mode emission byte-identical (corpus-diff, 111 files); no cache-generation bump needed.

Measured: zz2.pl repro 1/1 both calls = perl; eval.t 114 (pre-flip baseline) → 121 passing, fail set row-identical to the blessed baseline; Pl/t 138/5092 PASS; full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18498 → 18506 (+8). Normative: ir-spec §9.1 "pad-chain continuation" block; DECIDED.md line; guard row in Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t (fred1/fred2/nested + my-$fact factorial with local-of-global in eval mode).
